mainTopic: What the word 'אותו' teaches about slaughter in the north, followed by lashes for baking a חמץ מנחה and bloodletting from a sick בכור.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a series of דרשות on the פסוק about the נשיא's goat: 'השעיר' includes the goats for עבודה זרה in סמיכה. רבינא and מר זוטרא then show that the word 'אותו' cannot be excluding נחשון's goat from the north. There was never a reason to think it needed the north, because we do not learn a one-time offering (שעה) from offerings for all generations (דורות). The גמרא tries other jobs for 'אותו': the slaughterer need not stand in the north, a bird is not killed in the north, and the פסח is not slaughtered in the north. Each one is pushed back, either because another source already teaches it or because the קל וחומר behind it breaks down. In the end the גמרא returns to its first reading: the animal must be in the north, but the slaughterer need not be. It rereads רבי אחייה as teaching that the one who collects the blood must stand in the north. Next the גמרא explains רב פפא's rule that baking a חמץ מנחה can bring two sets of lashes, depending on whether the baker also shaped the dough. The amud closes with a ברייתא on bleeding a sick בכור: רבי מאיר forbids making a מום, the חכמים allow it, and רבי שמעון's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'the goat' includes goats for idol worship in סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its דרשה: the word 'השעיר' teaches that the goats brought as communal חטאות for עבודה זרה need סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'the goat' comes to include the goats brought for idol worship in the מצוה of leaning hands on the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching from the פסוק about the נשיא's goat. The extra word 'השעיר' adds the goats brought for עבודה זרה to the מצוה of סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes a series of דרשות on one פסוק. Each word teaches something. Here the word 'the goat' widens the rule of סמיכה to cover another type of goat חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to add something to a rule
The goats brought as communal sin offerings when the community sinned with idol worship
Leaning one's hands with full weight on the animal's head before slaughtering it

phrases.english: To include the goats of idol worship in placing hands.
phrases.notes: This is explaining the word 'השעיר' (the goat) from ויקרא 4:24.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבּוֹת שְׂעִירֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לִסְמִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a series of דרשות that began before this part of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The goats brought for עבודה זרה require סמיכה, learned from the word 'השעיר'.

steps.title: רבינא asks why רבי שמעון would need the exclusion
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the earlier דרשה that excluded נחשון's goat from slaughter in the north. It fits רבי יהודה, but not רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: this works for רבי יהודה, but what can we say according to רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the earlier teaching that the word 'אותו' excludes נחשון's goat from being slaughtered in the north. He asks why רבי שמעון would need such an exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that נחשון's goat needed סמיכה. Because of that, one might have thought it also needed slaughter in the north, so the exclusion is useful for him. רבי שמעון gives נחשון's goat no special inclusion, so there was never a reason to think it needed the north, and the exclusion seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it; a strong objection to what was just said
This works well for...
What is there to say? (meaning: there seems to be no good answer)

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it:
It works out well according to Rabbi Yehuda,
but according to Rabbi Shimon, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא תִּינַח לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the exclusion of נחשון's goat taught in the same series of דרשות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The דרשה that 'אותו' excludes נחשון's goat from slaughter in the north.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An exclusion is only needed if we might have thought otherwise. For רבי שמעון there is no reason to think so, so the word seems unnecessary.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: even for רבי יהודה the question stands
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא tells רבינא that the question applies to רבי יהודה as well. Including נחשון's goat in סמיכה does not automatically include it in slaughter in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said to רבינא: even for רבי יהודה, what was included is included, and what was not included is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא makes רבינא's question stronger. He says that even for רבי יהודה there was no reason to think נחשון's goat needed the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed that once סמיכה applies, we might also think north applies. מר זוטרא rejects that link: an inclusion covers only what it explicitly includes. So the exclusion of the north looks unneeded for both תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Also; as well
It was included (by a word in the פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina:
According to Rabbi Yehuda as well,
what was included was included,
phrases.notes: He means סמיכה, which רבי יהודה did include for נחשון's goat.

phrases.english: and what was not included was not included.
phrases.notes: He means slaughter in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי מַאי דְּאִיתְרַבִּי אִיתְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רבינא's challenge so that it applies to רבי יהודה too.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's assumption that the exclusion is needed according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being included in one rule (סמיכה) gives no reason to think another rule (north) applies. So the exclusion is unnecessary even for רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A possible answer: we would have learned the north from a בנין אב
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא raises a possible answer himself: without the exclusion, we would have learned slaughter in the north for נחשון's goat from a בנין אב of all other חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: if the פסוק had not excluded it, I would have said to derive it through a בנין אב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer that could save the exclusion. It is setting this answer up so it can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that every regular חטאת is slaughtered in the north. So without a word excluding it, we would have applied the same rule to נחשון's goat through a בנין אב. This would explain why the exclusion was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא brings up a possible answer, usually to reject it)
Excluded it
I would have thought
Learning a general rule from a model case and applying it to similar cases

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא, אִי לָא מַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא,
phrases.english: And if you will say: had the verse not excluded it,
I would have said: let it be derived through a paradigm,
phrases.notes: He means learning slaughter in the north for נחשון's goat from all the regular חטאות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא אִי לָא מַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of the exclusion against מר זוטרא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested answer that is later rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exclusion seems pointless, since nothing would make us think נחשון's goat needs the north.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the exclusion, a בנין אב from regular חטאות would have required the north.

steps.title: If so, סמיכה should also come from a בנין אב
steps.stepSummary: The suggested answer is rejected. If a בנין אב could teach the north, it could also teach סמיכה, so the פסוק would not have needed to include סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should have stayed silent about סמיכה itself, and we would derive it through a בנין אב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from the last step. The same בנין אב would also have taught סמיכה, yet the פסוק had to include סמיכה with its own word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the תורה needed a word to include סמיכה for נחשון's goat shows that a בנין אב does not work for it. So the בנין אב could not have taught the north either, and the exclusion is still unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself
Let the פסוק stay silent about it

phrases.english: Then placing hands itself: let the verse be silent about it,
and let it be derived through a paradigm!

steps.triggerLanguage: סְמִיכָה גּוּפַהּ לִישְׁתּוֹק קְרָא מִינֵּיהּ וְתֵיתֵי בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the בנין אב answer from step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects fully the idea that a בנין אב would have taught the north.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If a בנין אב worked here, the פסוק's separate inclusion of סמיכה would be unneeded.

steps.title: We do not learn a one-time offering from offerings for all generations
steps.stepSummary: The real reason a בנין אב fails is that נחשון's goat was a one-time offering, and we do not learn it from permanent offerings. This applies to the north just as it does to סמיכה, so מר זוטרא's question stays standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we do not learn a one-time offering from offerings for all generations. Here too, we do not learn a one-time offering from offerings for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason the בנין אב cannot work. A one-time offering cannot be learned from regular offerings, and that blocks learning the north just as it blocks learning סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחשון's goat was brought only once, at the inauguration of the משכן (שעה). Regular חטאות are for all generations (דורות). Since this rule blocks any בנין אב for the north, there was never a reason to think נחשון's goat needed the north, and the question on the exclusion remains.

keyTerms.meaning: A one-time situation, like the offerings at the משכן's inauguration
Rules that apply for all generations
We do not learn (one case from another)
Here too; the same applies in this case

steps.whatToRemember: Key rule: שעה מדורות לא ילפינן. A one-time offering (like נחשון's at the משכן's inauguration) cannot be learned from offerings meant for all generations. So the north requirement could never have reached נחשון's goat.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this step answers רבינא's question. It actually blocks the possible answer, so the question on the exclusion of the north stays strong.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule שעה מדורות לא ילפינן is a general principle that the גמרא uses in many places to keep one-time events apart from permanent law.

phrases.english: Rather, we do not learn the temporary from the permanent.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'a time from generations.' נחשון's offering was a one-time event; regular חטאות are for all generations.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, שָׁעָה מִדּוֹרוֹת לָא יָלְפִינַן.
phrases.english: Here too, we do not learn the temporary from the permanent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שָׁעָה מִדּוֹרוֹת לָא יָלְפִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the בנין אב fails, and applies that reason to the north as well.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because we do not learn שעה from דורות, nothing would have made נחשון's goat need the north. So מר זוטרא's challenge stands for רבי יהודה as well.

steps.title: A new job for the word: the animal in the north, not the slaughterer
steps.stepSummary: Since אוֹתוֹ cannot exclude נחשון's goat, the גמרא suggests it teaches that the animal must be in the north, while the person slaughtering does not have to stand there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, "it" (the animal) needs to be in the north, but the one slaughtering does not need to stand in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The old explanation of the word אוֹתוֹ fell apart. Now the גמרא offers a different thing this word could be teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אוֹתוֹ is still treated as a limiting word. Now it limits the north requirement to the animal itself and leaves out the שוחט's position. So the north rule is about where the animal is, not where the person stands.

keyTerms.meaning: "It". A limiting word: only it, and not something else
Requires the north side of the עזרה
The one who slaughters the animal

phrases.english: Rather,
"it" requires the north,
but the one slaughtering does not stand in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אוֹתוֹ טָעוּן צָפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 6 left the old reading of אוֹתוֹ refuted, this step suggests a new purpose for the word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the extra word to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word אוֹתוֹ was needed to exclude נחשון's goat
steps.terutzMaskana: The word אוֹתוֹ teaches that only the animal must be in the north, not the slaughterer

steps.title: That rule already comes from רבי אחייה's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we already know the slaughterer need not stand in the north from רבי אחייה's ברייתא on the עולה פסוק, so אוֹתוֹ here is not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is already learned from רבי אחייה! As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אחייה says, "And he shall slaughter it on the side of the altar northward." Why does the פסוק say "it"? We found that the one receiving the blood stands in the north and receives in the north, and if he stood in the south and received in the north it is invalid. You might think the slaughterer is the same. So the פסוק says "it": it, the animal, must be in the north, but the slaughterer does not need to stand in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from step 7. It quotes a ברייתא showing that this exact rule is already learned from a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחייה learns from the אוֹתוֹ in the עולה פסוק that the slaughterer may stand outside the north. He contrasts this with the one receiving the blood, who must stand in the north. Since the rule is already known, the אוֹתוֹ by the שעיר of the נשיא would be extra if it only taught this again.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן who catches the blood in a vessel
Why did the פסוק need to say this?
"One might think". Introduces a possible mistaken idea that the פסוק comes to block
Invalid (the offering is disqualified)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different פסוקים with the word אוֹתוֹ. רבי אחייה's is about the עולה (ויקרא 1:11). The one being explained in this sugya is about the שעיר of the נשיא. The question is that one source already covers the rule, so the other word must teach something else.

phrases.english: That is derived from Rabbi Achiya!
As it is taught: Rabbi Achiya says:
"And he shall slaughter it on the side of the altar northward,"
why does the verse say this?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the extra word "it" is there.

phrases.english: Since we have found regarding the one receiving the blood
that he stands in the north and receives in the north,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עָמַד בְּדָרוֹם וְקִיבֵּל בַּצָּפוֹן – פָּסוּל,
phrases.english: and if he stood in the south and received in the north, it is invalid,
one might think this one is also so?
The verse says: "it":
it must be in the north,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הַשּׁוֹחֵט צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת עוֹמֵד בַּצָּפוֹן!
phrases.english: but the slaughterer does not need to be standing in the north!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבִּי אֲחִיָּיה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 7's proposed teaching as already known from another source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that אוֹתוֹ by the שעיר of the נשיא teaches that the slaughterer need not stand in the north
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already learned from רבי אחייה's reading of אוֹתוֹ in the עולה פסוק, so this word would be extra.

steps.title: The word excludes a bird offering from the north
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests that אוֹתוֹ teaches the goat needs the north but a bird offering does not. Without it, we might have required the north for a bird through a קל וחומר from a sheep. The next step rejects this suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: "it" must be in the north, but a bird does not need the north. You might have thought to learn a bird from a sheep by a קל וחומר: a sheep, for which the תורה did not require a כהן, still requires the north. A bird, for which the תורה did require a כהן, should surely require the north too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for what אוֹתוֹ teaches: it leaves birds out of the north rule. Then it explains why we would have needed this word, by showing the mistaken קל וחומר we might have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep's slaughter does not have to be done by a כהן, yet it must be in the north. A bird must be killed by a כהן, which seems like the stricter rule. So logic would say a bird should also need the north. The word אוֹתוֹ blocks this conclusion, so the word is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as an offering
A sheep or goat brought as an offering
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one
"It would enter your mind". Introduces a mistaken first thought
The תורה fixed that a כהן must do it

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a proposal. The suggestion is that אוֹתוֹ excludes a bird from the north, to block a קל וחומר from a sheep (no כהן needed, yet north required) to a bird (כהן required). The next step knocks the קל וחומר down, so this reading does not stand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא. When a limiting word seems extra, the גמרא finds a mistaken logical argument that the word comes to block.

phrases.english: Rather: it must be in the north,
but a bird does not need the north.
It would enter your mind to say:
let it be learned by a kal vachomer from a sheep:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בֶּן צֹאן שֶׁלָּא קָבַע לוֹ כֹּהֵן
phrases.english: if a sheep, for which the Torah did not fix a priest,
phrases.notes: A sheep may be slaughtered by a non-כהן.

phrases.english: still had the north fixed for it,
then a bird, for which it did fix a priest,
is it not logical that we should fix the north for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אוֹתוֹ בַּצָּפוֹן, וְאֵין בֶּן עוֹף בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 knocks out step 7's suggestion, this step gives another purpose for אוֹתוֹ and explains why it is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the extra word to block a mistaken קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bird would need the north, learned by a קל וחומר from a sheep
steps.terutzMaskana: The word אוֹתוֹ limits the north requirement to the animal and leaves out a bird offering

steps.title: A sheep is different because it needs a knife
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר from a sheep to a bird is refuted. A sheep must be slaughtered with a utensil, but a bird is not, so we could never have learned the bird from the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a sheep? It is special, because the תורה requires a utensil for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from Step 9. The קל וחומר from a sheep to a bird does not work, so אוֹתוֹ is not needed to block it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep must be slaughtered with a knife, while a bird offering is killed by hand without a utensil. Because a sheep has this special feature, we cannot assume a bird shares the sheep's north rule. With no real הוה אמינא to block, אוֹתוֹ cannot be there to exclude the bird.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about X? It is special because…' This is the standard way to break a קל וחומר by showing the source case is unique.
A sheep (a member of the flock).
A utensil. Here it means the knife needed for slaughter.
The תורה fixed or set a requirement for it.

phrases.english: What about a sheep?
phrases.notes: This answers Step 9, where we thought we might learn the bird from the sheep.

phrases.english: It is special, because the Torah fixed a utensil for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְבֶן צֹאן, שֶׁכֵּן קָבַע לוֹ כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר that Step 9 relied on, so Step 9's answer falls.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that אוֹתוֹ excludes a bird offering from the north.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קל וחומר from a sheep fails, because a sheep has a special stringency (it needs a utensil) that a bird lacks.

steps.title: Maybe אוֹתוֹ excludes the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: A new suggestion: אוֹתוֹ teaches that the king's goat needs the north, but the קרבן פסח does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'it' is slaughtered in the north, but the פסח is not slaughtered in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new answer for what אוֹתוֹ excludes: the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אוֹתוֹ limits the north rule to this goat, so the פסח would not need to be slaughtered in the north. This is a fresh attempt to give the extra word a job.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals a new answer after the previous one failed.
The קרבן פסח, the Passover offering.
The north side of the עזרה, where the most holy offerings are slaughtered.

phrases.english: Rather: "it" is in the north,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the king's goat, the חטאת this פסוק is about.

phrases.english: but the Paschal offering is not in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: ״אוֹתוֹ״ בַּצָּפוֹן, וְאֵין פֶּסַח בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bird suggestion is rejected, a new exclusion is proposed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New exclusion assigned to the extra word אוֹתוֹ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the פסח also needs the north.
steps.terutzMaskana: אוֹתוֹ limits the north rule to the goat, excluding the פסח.

steps.title: The פסח rule already comes from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we already know the פסח does not need the north from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so this אוֹתוֹ is not needed for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule about the פסח is derived from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 11. The פסח exclusion already has a different source, so our אוֹתוֹ would be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of attack as in Step 8: a word cannot be 'used up' teaching something we already know from elsewhere. The source is about to be quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived (literally, 'it comes out') from a source.

phrases.aramaic: פֶּסַח מִדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: The Paschal offering is derived from Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov's teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֶּסַח מִדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 11's answer by pointing to an existing source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אוֹתוֹ excludes the פסח from the north.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That exclusion is already learned from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so this אוֹתוֹ would be unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's קל וחומר from an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is quoted. One might think the פסח needs the north through a קל וחומר: an עולה has no fixed time yet needs the north, so the פסח, which has a fixed time, should surely need the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, might the פסח need the north? It seems logical. If an עולה, which has no set time for its slaughter, still needs the north, then surely the פסח, which does have a set time for its slaughter, should need the north!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it just mentioned, to show where the פסח rule comes from. Here we see the קל וחומר that the ברייתא considers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a fixed time is treated as a sign of importance. If the less 'time-bound' עולה needs the north, the time-bound פסח should need it even more. This is the reasoning the ברייתא sets up so that it can then exclude the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think…' It introduces a possible mistaken assumption.
Requires.
'And it is logical.' It introduces a reasoned argument, here a קל וחומר.
A burnt offering, which needs the north.
A fixed time. The פסח must be slaughtered on the afternoon of the fourteenth of ניסן.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Might the Paschal offering require the north?
And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עוֹלָה שֶׁלָּא קָבַע לָהּ זְמַן בִּשְׁחִיטָתָהּ
phrases.english: If a burnt offering, for which the Torah did not fix a time for its slaughter,
still had the north fixed for it,
then the Paschal offering, for which the Torah fixed a time for its slaughter,
is it not logical that the north is fixed for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source mentioned in Step 12's objection.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסח's exclusion from the north already has its own source.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: An עולה is special because it is fully burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's קל וחומר: an עולה is entirely burned on the מזבח, so we cannot learn the פסח from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an עולה? It is special, because it is entirely burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא breaks the קל וחומר in the ברייתא by pointing out a special feature of an עולה. The next steps check whether a different offering could serve as the source instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is completely burned on the מזבח, which makes it more stringent than a פסח, which is eaten. So the עולה's north rule cannot be carried over to the פסח. If the קל וחומר fails, there was never a real reason to think the פסח needs the north, so no word in the פסוק is needed to exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: Entirely burned. Nothing of the animal is eaten; all of it goes on the מזבח.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two refutations. In Step 10 the special feature was the sheep's knife; here it is the עולה being fully burned. Both use the same 'מָה לְ… שֶׁכֵּן' pattern to break a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: What about a burnt offering?
It is special, because it is entirely burned!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְעוֹלָה, שֶׁכֵּן כָּלִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר quoted in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ברייתא's קל וחומר from an עולה to the פסח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An עולה has a unique stringency (it is entirely burned) that the פסח lacks.

steps.title: The פסח cannot be learned from a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: Trying to learn the פסח from a חטאת fails, because a חטאת atones for sins that carry כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to learn it from a חטאת, that fails too. A חטאת is special because it atones for sins that carry the punishment of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps testing the ברייתא's קל וחומר and now tries a חטאת as the source. It rejects that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is not entirely burned, so the problem raised against the עולה in step 14 does not apply here. But a חטאת has its own special power: it atones for very serious sins that carry כרת. The פסח has no such power, so we cannot say 'if a חטאת needs the north, surely the פסח does.'

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering
Sins that carry the punishment of כרת (being cut off)
"What about X? It is special because..." This is the standard way to knock down a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: From a sin offering? What about a sin offering?
It is special in that it atones for sins punishable by כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחַטָּאת – מָה לְחַטָּאת שֶׁכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the refutation from step 14 by trying a second possible source, the חטאת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects building the ברייתא's קל וחומר from a חטאת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A חטאת has an extra strength the פסח lacks: it atones for sins punishable by כרת.

steps.title: Not from a guilt offering, nor from any of them
steps.stepSummary: Trying to learn the פסח from an אשם also fails, because an אשם is קדשי קדשים. That point knocks out all three sources at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to learn it from an אשם, that fails too. An אשם is special because it is one of the holiest offerings. In fact, you cannot learn it from any of them, since they are all among the holiest offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more source, the אשם, and rejects it. Then it points out that one reason blocks all three sources together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is not fully burned and does not atone for כרת, so the earlier objections do not apply to it. But it is קדשי קדשים, and the פסח is only קדשים קלים. The עולה, the חטאת and the אשם all share this higher holiness, so none of them can teach us about the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering
The highest level of offerings, the most holy
"From all of them too": one objection that covers every source

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's קל וחומר for the פסח cannot be built from the עולה, the חטאת or the אשם. All of them are קדשי קדשים, and the פסח is not. So there was never a reason to think the פסח needs the north, and אוֹתוֹ cannot be there to exclude it. That is why the גמרא goes back to its first reading in the next step.

phrases.english: From a guilt offering? What about a guilt offering?
It is special in that it is of the most holy offerings.
From all of them too it fails, since they are all of the most holy offerings.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the עולה, the חטאת and the אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאָשָׁם – מָה לְאָשָׁם שֶׁכֵּן קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the refutation from steps 14 and 15 with the last source, then gives one reason that covers all three.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the אשם as a source, and then all three sources together.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The עולה, the חטאת and the אשם are all קדשי קדשים, which the פסח is not.

steps.title: Back to the first reading; רבי אחייה teaches about the one who collects the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its first reading: the animal must be in the north, but the slaughterer need not be. רבי אחייה's teaching is really about the person who collects the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is really as we said at first: "it" must be in the north, but the slaughterer does not need to be in the north. You asked why we need this if we already know it from רבי אחייה. The answer is that רבי אחייה did not come to tell us that the slaughterer may stand outside the north. Rather, he is saying: the slaughterer need not be in the north, but the one who collects the blood must be in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the new suggestion about the פסח and goes back to its original explanation of אוֹתוֹ. It then answers the old objection by reading רבי אחייה in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old objection was that אוֹתוֹ is not needed to teach that the slaughterer may stand outside the north, since רבי אחייה already teaches that. The גמרא now answers that this point really comes from אוֹתוֹ. רבי אחייה's real new point is the other half of his statement: the one who collects the blood must stand in the north.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather, really...": going back to an earlier answer
At first, originally
The one who slaughters
The one who collects the blood in a vessel
To exclude

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אחייה's words do not change. The גמרא only changes which half of his statement is his real new point: the part about the one who collects the blood, not the part about the slaughterer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new rule that will be questioned right away: the one who collects the blood must stand in the north.

phrases.english: Rather, really it is as we said at first:
"It" must be in the north, but the slaughterer need not be in the north.
And what was difficult for you,
that this is already derived from רבי אחייה,
the teaching of רבי אחייה is not to exclude
the slaughterer from standing in the north, which is what you assumed he came for.
Rather, this is what he is saying:
The slaughterer need not be in the north,
but the one who collects the blood must be in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם כִּדְקָאָמְרִינַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the פסח suggestion is set aside (steps 14–16), the גמרא returns to the first reading of אוֹתוֹ from step 7 and answers step 8's objection from רבי אחייה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads רבי אחייה so that his new point is about the one who collects the blood, not the slaughterer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אחייה came to teach that the slaughterer may stand outside the north, which would make that use of אוֹתוֹ unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: אוֹתוֹ teaches that the slaughterer need not be in the north. רבי אחייה teaches that the one who collects the blood must be in the north.
steps.kashyaTarget: The old objection that אוֹתוֹ is not needed because of רבי אחייה.

steps.title: Collecting in the north is already known from "and he shall take"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rule for the one who collects the blood is already learned from the extra ו in ״וְלָקַח״.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the rule for the one who collects the blood comes from "take" versus "and he shall take"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 17. The rule about collecting the blood already has a source, so why would רבי אחייה be needed for it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written "take" but wrote "and he shall take." The extra ו links the collecting to the north. If this is already the source, רבי אחייה cannot be the one who teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall take" (the extra ו is used to teach a rule)
"It comes out from": it is derived from

phrases.english: The rule for the one who collects is derived from "take" versus "and he shall take"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:34. The point is the extra letter ו at the start of the word.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְקַבֵּל מִ״לָּקַח״ ״וְלָקַח״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading of רבי אחייה given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אחייה teaches that the one who collects the blood must be in the north.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule already has a source, the extra ו in ״וְלָקַח״, so it would be repeated for no reason.

steps.title: This תנא does not learn from the extra ו
steps.stepSummary: The תנא here does not learn anything from "take" versus "and he shall take," so he needs רבי אחייה's source for the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not learn anything from "take" versus "and he shall take."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. This תנא does not use the extra ו to learn any rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning a rule from an extra ו is a method some תנאים use and others do not. Since this תנא does not use it, he needs a different source for the rule about the one who collects. That source is the teaching of רבי אחייה.

keyTerms.meaning: "It does not mean anything to him": he does not learn anything from it

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: אוֹתוֹ teaches that the slaughterer need not be in the north. רבי אחייה teaches that the one who collects the blood must be in the north, because this תנא does not learn from the ו of ״וְלָקַח״.

phrases.english: "Take" versus "and he shall take" means nothing to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לָקַח״ ״וְלָקַח״ לָא מַשְׁמַע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different תנאים use different ways of learning from the פסוק: this תנא does not learn from an extra ו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone learns the rule for the one who collects from the ו of ״וְלָקַח״, which would make רבי אחייה's teaching unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא does not learn from the ו, so he needs רבי אחייה's source for the rule about the one who collects.

steps.title: רב פפא: baking can bring two sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of acts that bring lashes for making a מנחה into חמץ. רב פפא adds that baking brings two sets of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a person is liable for kneading the מנחה, for shaping it, and for baking it. רב פפא said: if he baked it, he gets two sets of lashes, one for shaping and one for baking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about lashes for making a מנחה into חמץ, and רב פפא adds a new rule about baking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three separate acts: kneading, shaping, and baking. רב פפא says the act of baking counts twice. It brings lashes for baking and also lashes for shaping.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneading the dough
Shaping the dough into its form
Baking
Gets lashes

phrases.english: And one is liable for kneading it,
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from the משנה. "It" is a מנחה that was made into חמץ.

phrases.english: and for shaping it, and for baking it.
Rav Pappa said:
If he baked it, he is flogged twice,
once for shaping it,
and once for baking it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפָאָהּ – לוֹקֶה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's list of acts that bring lashes for a חמץ מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Baking a מנחה as חמץ brings two sets of lashes, one for shaping and one for baking.

steps.title: But baking was called a single act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא from a ברייתא that describes baking as one single act with its own liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said: just as baking is special in that it is a single act and one is liable for it by itself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's rule using a line from a ברייתא it quoted earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls baking 'a single act' that brings liability by itself. That sounds like one set of lashes for baking, not two. This seems to contradict רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Special, having its own feature
A single act
By itself, on its own

phrases.english: But you said:
phrases.notes: This refers to a ברייתא quoted earlier in this sugya, which learns other cases from baking.

phrases.english: Just as baking is special
in that it is a single act
and one is liable for it by itself?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמְרַתְּ: מָה אֲפִיָּיה מְיוּחֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's rule from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that baking brings two sets of lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls baking a single act with its own liability, which suggests only one set of lashes.

steps.title: Same baker versus a different baker
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks of one person who shaped and baked. רב פפא speaks of someone who bakes dough that another person shaped.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. The ברייתא is about a case where he himself shaped it and he himself baked it. רב פפא is about a case where his friend shaped it, gave it to him, and he baked it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא and רב פפא are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the same person shaped and then baked, he already got lashes for shaping, so baking adds only one more. If someone else shaped it, the baker gets two sets of lashes, because his baking also finishes the shaping. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources speak of different cases
His friend, another person

steps.whatToRemember: One person who shapes and bakes gets one set of lashes for each act. A person who bakes dough that someone else shaped gets two sets of lashes for the baking.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where he shaped it and he baked it,
phrases.notes: "This" means the ברייתא. The same person did both acts.

phrases.english: that is where his friend shaped it
and gave it to him, and he baked it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דַּעֲרַךָ הוּא וַאֲפָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one person versus two people)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Baking always brings only one set of lashes, so רב פפא is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of one person doing both acts. רב פפא speaks of baking dough that someone else shaped.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: letting blood from a sick firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a בכור sick from too much blood may be bled only in a spot that does not cause a מום, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: a בכור that is sick with too much blood may have blood let in a place that does not cause a מום. We may not let its blood in a place that causes a מום. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about letting blood from a sick בכור, starting with רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We may not make a מום in a בכור on purpose. So רבי מאיר allows bloodletting to save the animal only where it will not leave a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn kosher animal, which belongs to the כהן
Sick from too much blood
Letting blood (cutting to release blood)
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A firstborn animal that is seized by blood,
phrases.notes: The animal is sick from blood buildup, and only bloodletting can help it.

phrases.english: we may let its blood
in a place where it does not make a blemish in it,
but we may not let the blood
in a place where it makes a blemish in it.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוֹר שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about causing a מום in a בכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a sick בכור may be bled only in a spot that does not cause a מום.

steps.title: The חכמים allow bleeding even where it causes a blemish
steps.stepSummary: חכמים allow bloodletting even where it causes a מום, but the animal may not be slaughtered because of that מום. רבי שמעון begins his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: he may let blood even in a place that causes a מום, as long as he does not slaughter the animal because of that מום. רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר and allow the bloodletting, with one condition. Then the גמרא sets up רבי שמעון's view, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בכור with a lasting מום may be slaughtered and eaten. The חכמים allow the cut to save the animal. But a מום that came from this cut does not count as a reason to slaughter it.

keyTerms.meaning: He may let blood
As long as, provided that
He will slaughter

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: he may let blood
even in a place where it makes a blemish in it,
as long as he does not slaughter it
on account of that blemish.
Rabbi Shimon says:

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: יַקִּיז, אַף בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשִׂין בּוֹ מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's opinion, which disagrees with רבי מאיר in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: bloodletting is allowed even where it causes a מום, but that מום may not be used as the reason to slaughter the animal.
